summary: Adds a novel top-level command `garmin-pp-cli sql <query>` (internal/cli/garmin_sql.go, internal/cli/garmin_sql_test.go), registered on the root command beside `insights` with one AddCommand line and a comment at internal/cli/root.go, and lifts the MCP sql tool's statement gate into a new hand-owned package internal/sqlguard so the command and the tool enforce one contract. WHY THE PRESS CANNOT EXPRESS THIS: the press emits `sql` only as an MCP tool (internal/mcp/tools.go registers it with handleSQL); there is no generated CLI verb, and the two generated CLI read paths over the archive are `analytics` (count or group one resource type by one top-level JSON field) and `search` (FTS5 text match). Neither can express an arbitrary aggregate, a join across two series, or json_extract on a nested path. WHAT IT DOES: runs exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT against the local archive, read-only; the query makes no network call (the root --deliver flag, as on every command, may post the finished envelope after it returns). Output goes through the same helpers the generated commands use (wantsHumanTable, printJSONFiltered), so --json, --agent, --compact, --csv, --plain, --quiet and --select behave identically to every generated command; a TTY gets the tab-separated table in the query's own column order. --db defaults through garminArchivePath, the same resolver `insights` and `history` use, so --home and GARMIN_HOME are honoured. Deadline and row budget are the MCP tool's own bound.WithSQLQueryDeadline and bound.NewSQLScanState (SQLMaxRows 10000, MaxBytes 60000); a bounded result sets truncated:true, the cap that actually stopped the scan (max_bytes, or max_rows when the row backstop is what fired) and note in the envelope rather than silently returning a short answer. The envelope is this command's own shape, not a field-for-field mirror of the MCP tool's, which carries store_status, resumable and returned_count instead. THREE LAYERS, NONE TRUSTED ALONE: (1) internal/sqlguard.Validate refuses anything that is not a single SELECT or WITH statement, after stripping the leading whitespace, line comments, block comments and semicolons SQLite itself skips — so `-- x\nDROP TABLE resources`, `/* x */ DROP ...` and `SELECT 1; ATTACH ...` are refused, not just bare DROP. (2) The handle is opened mode=ro with _pragma=query_only(true), so the CTE-wrapped write the gate deliberately does not parse (`WITH x AS (...) INSERT ...`) answers SQLITE_READONLY. (3) Added in N131.5.6 for the CLI verb and extended to the MCP sql tool in N131.7.4: the query runs on one *sql.Conn that carries SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH = 4 MiB, so an oversized computed value such as hex(zeroblob(100000000)) or group_concat(data) over the whole archive is refused by SQLite (SQLITE_TOOBIG) before it is allocated — the generated bound.SQLScanState marshals a row before comparing it to its 60000-byte budget, so without this layer one value cost 1.32 GB of RSS at exit 0 with truncated:true. The cap is per VALUE, not per row: a row of many values each under the cap is still marshalled whole. 4 MiB rather than a budget-sized cap because the limit also refuses any read that touches a stored value above it, and the largest archived row measured 145795 bytes. The cap, the boundary constant and the SQLITE_TOOBIG test live once in internal/sqlguard/cellcap.go (MaxCellBytes, CapConn, IsValueTooBig); internal/cli/garmin_sql.go keeps garminSQLMaxCellBytes, garminSQLConn and isSQLValueTooBig as delegating names because its own cases call them directly, and internal/mcp/tools.go handleSQL calls sqlguard.CapConn on the store's pool. POOL SIZE IS LOAD-BEARING on the MCP side: handleSQL holds the capped connection open past the scan loop while mcpStoreStatus reads on a second one, which store.OpenReadOnlyContext's SetMaxOpenConns(2) allows; at a pool of one that call would block rather than error. ONE DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT, AND IT IS NOT THE QUERY'S: resolving the default --db goes through garminArchivePath, the resolver `insights` and `history` share, which pins a data.db in a home that has none and renames a single token-scoped archive to the home's name; the store's own open then migrates that file, so a run in a fresh home leaves a migrated but empty archive behind — measured at 196608 bytes with 0 rows and no garmin_series_state, the same footprint `insights` leaves — and the read-only open then creates the usual -shm and an empty -wal beside it. That happens before the query runs, is the same behaviour every archive-reading command has, and is skipped entirely by --db. No archived row is changed on any path. Both layers are load-bearing and each is proved separately by test: mode=ro alone does NOT stop `ATTACH DATABASE` from creating a file (measured on modernc.org/sqlite v1.37.0, this build), and a prefix-only keyword check does not stop a leading comment. WAL: the handle deliberately omits immutable=1. store.OpenReadOnlyContext carried immutable=1 until N131.5.5 (see garmin-store-readonly-wal.json), so the two DSNs differed; they are now the same shape. On a WAL fixture with a writer connection open, mode=ro&immutable=1 was measured to report `no such table` for a table that exists and to miss a committed row that had not been checkpointed; plain mode=ro sees it. TestGarminSQLSeesUncheckpointedWALCommit asserts both halves so the difference stays attributable to the flag. N131.7.4 (upstream PR review, Greptile policy gate P1): the per-value cap was the CLI verb's alone, so the MCP sql tool — the surface an agent actually calls — ran the same oversized query on an uncapped pool connection. The cap moved to internal/sqlguard, where the statement gate already lived, and handleSQL now runs on a capped connection too.
reason: N131 decision D20 (owner, 2026-09-13): `insights` answers the two questions we knew to ask, and the largest benefit is in the questions we did not — an archive of years of daily series has no fixed recipe list. `sql` is the escape hatch that makes the archive worth filling for a question nobody anticipated, in the same 'Local state that compounds' group as `history`. It is hand-written rather than adapted from the espn CLI's `sql` verb because that verb's prefix-only keyword guard over a read-write handle was demonstrated to pass a CTE INSERT, REPLACE, ATTACH and VACUUM INTO (owner memory, 2026-08-22); that is the exact failure this build's two layers prevent, case by case, in TestGarminSQLBlastRadius.
call_sites: "topic": "Loopback browser login with identity assertion", "insight": "Every other client either takes your password

validated_outcome: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... exit 0, gofmt -l clean, go test -count=1 ./... green with 0 FAIL. TestGarminSQLBlastRadius runs eleven statements through the verb against a WAL fixture and sha256s the database file before and after each: a CTE INSERT, REPLACE, ATTACH, VACUUM INTO a scratch path, PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE, `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE resources`, a line-comment-hidden DROP, a block-comment-hidden DROP, writefile() and load_extension() are each refused with the bytes unchanged and no file created in the scratch directory; a plain SELECT returns its two rows. TestGarminSQLHandleRefusesWritesWithoutTheGate re-runs the write forms straight against the handle, bypassing the gate entirely, and asserts PRAGMA query_only is 1. TestGarminSQLRefusesAFlagAfterTheQuery pins the other silent shape: a flag written after the bare -- used to be joined onto the query as a SQL line comment, so the query ran and the flag was dropped at exit 0; it is now refused by name. TestMCPSQLGuardIsTheSharedGuard asserts handleSQL refuses with byte-identical wording to sqlguard.Validate, which is the only thing that catches a re-render silently un-sharing the gate. Empty and missing archives: a store with no rows answers zero rows at exit 0 with a stderr hint naming `garmin-pp-cli history --since all`, and an archive that has rows but no match for the query gets a different next_step naming the filter instead. LIVE: run against a populated archive — a resource_type census, a json_extract grouped by month over the activities series, and a join of the activities and activity_hr_zones series on the id they share all returned rows. N131.7.4 (MCP cap): gofmt -l . empty, go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... exit 0, go test -count=1 ./... 15 packages ok, 5 [no test files] and 0 FAIL, go mod tidy leaves go.mod and go.sum byte-identical. RED first, recorded before the handler edit: with handleSQL still on db.DB().QueryContext, TestMCPSQLRefusesAnOversizedComputedCell (both subtests), TestMCPSQLRefusesAnOversizedGroupConcat and TestMCPSQLRefusesAtTheSharedBoundary failed with 'an oversized cell was accepted' and the 200 OK envelope printed beside it — including the boundary case returning n = 4194320 at truncated:false. TestMCPSQLUnderCapStoredValueStillReadsWithStoreStatus was the positive control and passed both before and after, which is what shows the edit did not simply break the tool. New unit cases in internal/sqlguard cover CapConn setting the limit on the connection it returns (read back with sqlite.Limit -1), the boundary either side of MaxCellBytes, IsValueTooBig testing the result code rather than the text (a plain error quoting 'string or blob too big' is not claimed, a wrapped SQLITE_TOOBIG is), and 4 MiB clearing a 200 KB stored row through json_extract. No Garmin host was contacted and no real archive was opened: every fixture is a temp-dir store seeded in-process.
regen_notes: A re-render of internal/mcp/tools.go restores validateReadOnlyQuery, stripLeadingSQLNoise and hasTrailingSQLStatement inline and drops the internal/sqlguard import. That compiles and the CLI verb keeps working, so nothing fails loudly except internal/mcp/sql_shared_guard_test.go, which is the reason that file exists. Re-apply the three delegating bodies and the import after any dogfood/generate run, then run that test.

The command is registered AFTER the typed MCP sql tool in cmd/garmin-pp-mcp, so cobratree's walker sees s.GetTool("sql") != nil and skips the name rather than shadowing the typed tool (internal/mcp/cobratree/walker.go). A regen that reorders registration, or that stops emitting the typed sql tool, would turn `sql` into a shell-out mirror with a different contract. internal/mcp/tools_test.go already asserts the typed description survives; keep that assertion.

`sql` shares garminArchivePath, insightsSyncCommand, isMissingArchive and formatInsightValue with internal/cli/garmin_sync.go and internal/cli/garmin_insights.go. Those files are one novel unit: restoring this one without them does not compile.

The table list in the command's Long help is asserted against a freshly migrated store by TestGarminSQLHelpTablesExist, including garmin_series_state, which the windowed walk creates rather than the generated migration. A regen that renames a store table fails that test rather than shipping help that names a table the binary does not create.

FIXED IN N131.5.5 ROUND 2 (was: OPEN, NOT FIXED HERE) — store.OpenReadOnlyContext (internal/store/store.go) opened mode=ro&immutable=1, and openMCPReadOnlyStore (internal/mcp/tools.go) backs BOTH the MCP `sql` and `search` tools with it. On a WAL fixture with a writer connection open, that handle missed a committed row and reported `no such table` for a table that exists. immutable=1 is now dropped and query_only(true) added, so the store's DSN matches this command's; the change, its measured read-only-directory cost and the two generated tests it repaired are recorded in .printing-press-patches/garmin-store-readonly-wal.json.

The table list in the Long help says garmin_series_state is created by the first history run. A fresh home's migrated archive does not have it (measured this build), which is why TestGarminSQLHelpTablesExist calls EnsureGarminSeriesState before checking the list.

N131.5.6, CORRECTED N131.7.4 (the note here used to end 'The MCP sql tool still queries the pool uncapped'; it no longer does). The memory bound is now one constant and two helpers in internal/sqlguard/cellcap.go, reached from two call sites: garminSQLConn + the conn.QueryContext call in garminSQLQuery (internal/cli/garmin_sql.go), and the sqlguard.CapConn + conn.QueryContext pair in handleSQL (internal/mcp/tools.go). internal/sqlguard is hand-owned, so a reprint cannot touch the cap itself — only the two call sites.

N131.7.4 REGEN: a re-render of internal/mcp/tools.go restores handleSQL's db.DB().QueryContext(queryCtx, query) and drops both the sqlguard.CapConn block and mcpSQLQueryError's too-big branch. That compiles and the CLI verb keeps its own cap, so the only thing that fails loudly is internal/mcp/sql_cell_cap_test.go — TestMCPSQLRefusesAnOversizedComputedCell, TestMCPSQLRefusesAnOversizedGroupConcat and TestMCPSQLRefusesAtTheSharedBoundary go red with 'an oversized cell was accepted' and the envelope in the message. That file is hand-owned and lives outside the generated internal/mcp/tools_test.go for exactly that reason. Re-apply the two blocks (call_sites carries both needles verbatim) and run that file.

N131.7.4: handleSQL's capped connection stays checked out until the handler returns, while mcpStoreStatus(db) reads on a second connection from the same pool. store.OpenReadOnlyContext's SetMaxOpenConns(2) is what makes that legal. A regen or edit that lowers it to 1 makes handleSQL BLOCK rather than error, which is why TestMCPSQLUnderCapStoredValueStillReadsWithStoreStatus runs the handler off the test goroutine under a time budget instead of calling it inline.
